basic_information.name: Manus AI
basic_information.creator: Butterfly Effect (Monica.im / Beijing Butterfly Effect Technology Co., Ltd.), founded by CEO Xiao Hong and Chief Scientist Yichao 'Peak' Ji. Acquired by Meta Platforms in December 2025 for over $2 billion.
basic_information.release_date: March 6, 2025 (public launch). Company founded April 2022 as Monica.im.
basic_information.license: Proprietary (closed-source SaaS product). Note: OpenManus is a community-driven open-source recreation (MIT license) but is NOT the official product.
basic_information.current_version: Manus 1.6 (as of late 2025), which added mobile app development and 'Design View'. Previous major release was Manus 1.5 (October 2025) with 4x speed improvements.

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: multi_agent / orchestrator. Manus uses a multi-agent architecture with three coordinated sub-agents: a Planner Agent (decomposes problems into subtasks), an Execution Agent (carries out actions via tools and code), and a Verification Agent (validates outputs). These operate within an iterative agent loop: analyze -> plan -> execute -> observe.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Built on multiple LLMs: primarily Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet (v1) and Claude 3.7 for reasoning, plus fine-tuned versions of Alibaba's open-source Qwen models. The system is model-agnostic in design and can orchestrate across models. Manus is sometimes described as a 'Claude wrapper' because Claude Sonnet is the primary backbone for planning and execution.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Integrates approximately 29 external tools exposed via a structured tools.json configuration. Key tools include: browser automation (via Browser Use open-source library), shell_exec (command execution), file_read/file_saver (file management), code execution (Python, JavaScript, Bash), web search, and deployment tools. Since Manus 1.5, full MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector support enables integration with Gmail, Notion, Stripe, HubSpot, Slack, Google Calendar, Hugging Face, and many more. Tool orchestration follows the CodeAct paradigm where the agent generates and executes code snippets to invoke tools.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: hierarchical / code_as_plan. The Planner Agent decomposes user goals into a sequence of subtasks using hierarchical planning. Execution uses the CodeAct paradigm where the model generates executable Python code as its action mechanism, enabling flexible multi-step plans with conditional logic, loops, and library usage. A context-aware state machine manages tool availability, masking token logits during decoding to enforce or prevent certain actions based on current state.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Native multi-agent with manager pattern. Three specialized sub-agents (Planner, Executor, Verifier) coordinate via an event stream. The system supports parallelism where complex jobs are decomposed and components processed simultaneously. Team collaboration features (added in v1.5) allow multiple human users to join shared sessions.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term (conversation within a task session) | episodic (event stream logging all actions and observations) | semantic (knowledge retrieval from web and files). The event stream serves as working memory, capturing the full history of actions, observations, and intermediate results within a task.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Sophisticated KV-cache-optimized context engineering. Key strategies: (1) Stable prompt prefix to maximize KV-cache hits (cached tokens cost 0.30 USD/MTok vs 3 USD/MTok uncached for Claude — 10x difference); (2) Append-only context design that never modifies previous actions or observations; (3) Context-aware state machine for tool selection that masks logits during decoding; (4) Avoidance of timestamps in system prompts to preserve cache. The team rebuilt their agent framework four times to optimize context handling. Average input-to-output token ratio is approximately 100:1. Manus 1.5 expanded the context window for single tasks to handle larger/more complex problems.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: cloud. Tasks run asynchronously in E2B cloud-based sandboxes (Firecracker microVMs). State is persisted in the cloud sandbox environment during task execution. Users can check results asynchronously.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context engineering is treated as a first-class architectural concern — the Manus team considers the KV-cache hit rate the single most important metric for a production-stage AI agent. Published an influential blog post 'Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus' by co-founder Yichao Ji detailing their approach. Key principles: stable prefix for cache hits, append-only context, state-machine-based tool masking, and careful avoidance of cache-invalidating patterns (e.g., no timestamps in prompts).

capabilities.core_capabilities: General-purpose autonomous task execution across diverse domains: (1) Full-stack web application development and deployment (frontend, backend, databases, authentication, embedded AI); (2) Mobile app development (added in v1.6); (3) Data analysis and visualization (e.g., NBA scoring efficiency charts from player statistics); (4) Long-form research report generation with source synthesis; (5) Market research and competitive analysis; (6) Travel itinerary planning with budgets and accommodations; (7) Code generation, testing, and debugging across multiple languages; (8) Browser automation for web-based tasks; (9) File management and document processing; (10) Bibliographic research and academic cataloging; (11) One-click deployment of built applications. Achieved GAIA benchmark scores of 86.5% (basic), 70.1% (intermediate), 57.7% (complex), surpassing OpenAI's 74.3%, 69.1%, 47.6% respectively.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code (Python, JavaScript, Bash), browser (full web browsing and automation), file system (read/write/manage), shell/terminal, deployment, vision (screenshot analysis within browser). Mobile development added in v1.6.
capabilities.autonomy_level: fully_autonomous. Manus runs asynchronously in the cloud without requiring repeated prompts or human intervention. Users issue a goal and can check results later. The system plans, executes, verifies, and deploys independently. Some tasks run for extended periods (minutes to hours) in persistent sandbox sessions.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: 29+ built-in tools plus expandable MCP connector ecosystem. Built-in tools cover browser automation, shell execution, file operations, code execution, web search, and deployment. MCP connectors (from v1.5 onward) integrate with popular SaaS tools: Gmail, Notion, Stripe, HubSpot, Slack, Google Calendar, Hugging Face, and the broader MCP server ecosystem (1000+ community-contributed servers).

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Full MCP support since Manus 1.5. MCP connectors are prebuilt integrations connecting Manus to external tools and services. Supports both reading data from connected apps and performing actions within them. Official MCP documentation at manus.im/docs/integrations/mcp-connectors.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: No confirmed native A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol) support as of the latest version. The Google A2A protocol (announced April 2025) complements MCP with horizontal agent-to-agent communication, but Manus has not publicly announced A2A adoption. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: No confirmed AGENTS.md support. Manus operates as a managed SaaS product rather than a developer tool that reads project configuration files. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Moderate. Manus operates as a standalone managed product rather than an interoperable framework. However, MCP support enables integration with any MCP-compatible tool or service. The existence of a Manus MCP Server (by community contributor mantrakp04) suggests third parties can connect to Manus programmatically. Post-Meta acquisition, integration with Meta's AI ecosystem (including potential Avocado, OpenClaw integration) is expected.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: sandbox. All execution occurs within isolated E2B Firecracker microVM sandboxes — ephemeral, lightweight virtual machines that provide process and filesystem isolation. Ethical guardrails are enforced via system prompt instructions that prohibit harmful/illegal actions and prevent system prompt disclosure. This is essentially prompt-based governance combined with infrastructure-level sandboxing.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Limited explicit escalation. Manus is designed for fully autonomous operation. When the Verification Agent detects issues, it triggers re-planning within the agent loop. For user-facing scenarios, the 'Manus's Computer' interface provides real-time visibility into ongoing work, but the system does not proactively pause to ask for human approval before actions. [uncertain]
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Multi-layered approach: (1) Verification Agent that validates outputs after execution; (2) Code execution allows empirical verification of results rather than relying solely on LLM generation; (3) Web search for grounding in real data; (4) Integrated browser testing in v1.5 that tests built applications like a real user. However, known limitations exist: if data sources are flawed or the Verification Agent fails to catch errors, Manus can produce incorrect results confidently. No external fact-checking or citation verification system has been publicly documented.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Partial. Every action and result is logged in a structured event stream format. The 'Manus's Computer' interface provides real-time visibility into agent steps, tools used, and intermediate decisions. However, enterprise-grade audit and governance capabilities are noted as areas for future development.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: post_review. Manus operates autonomously by design. Users monitor progress via the 'Manus's Computer' real-time display showing agent actions. Results are reviewed after task completion. No pre-approval gates or confidence-threshold pauses are built into the standard workflow. Team collaboration features (v1.5) allow shared sessions but do not add approval gates.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: None. Manus is a proprietary commercial product. Now owned by Meta Platforms following the December 2025 acquisition. No standards body governance.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: MCP (Model Context Protocol) — Manus is an adopter/implementor of Anthropic's MCP standard for tool integration. Manus's success helped popularize MCP adoption across the AI agent ecosystem.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: Uncertain/under review. The Meta acquisition is under active regulatory scrutiny by Chinese authorities (Ministry of Commerce) examining compliance with export controls, technology transfer rules, cross-border data transfers, currency flows, and tax accounting. No public EU AI Act, SOC2, or HIPAA compliance certifications have been announced. Data privacy concerns exist given the Chinese origin and Singapore relocation. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: managed_service / cloud. Manus runs entirely as a cloud-hosted SaaS product. Agent execution occurs in E2B Firecracker microVM sandboxes in the cloud. No self-hosted or on-premise deployment option is publicly available.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: horizontal / serverless. E2B Firecracker microVMs spin up on demand (<200ms initialization) and run as ephemeral sandboxes. Each task gets its own isolated VM. The infrastructure scales horizontally with demand. E2B estimates building equivalent infrastructure from scratch would require 3-5 full-time infra engineers.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Estimated approximately $2 per task during early access phase. E2B sandbox costs approximately $0.067/hour for a small VM (1 vCPU, 1 GiB RAM). With the 100:1 input-to-output token ratio and Claude Sonnet pricing ($3/MTok uncached, $0.30/MTok cached), context engineering and KV-cache optimization significantly reduce per-task LLM costs. Subscription pricing: Plus plan $39/month, Pro plan $199/month (some sources cite $99/month Base and $499/month Pro with unlimited usage), Enterprise plan with custom pricing.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: No local hardware requirements for end users (cloud SaaS). Backend infrastructure runs on E2B's managed Firecracker microVM platform. Each sandbox provides a full virtual Linux environment with Python, JavaScript, Bash, browser, and deployment capabilities.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Built-in 'Manus's Computer' interface provides real-time monitoring of agent execution, showing active tools, steps taken, and intermediate results. No publicly documented integration with external observability platforms (LangSmith, Langfuse, etc.). [uncertain]
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — structured event stream logging captures every action, observation, and result in the agent loop. The 'Manus's Computer' view serves as a visual trace. Whether execution traces are exportable or queryable via API is not publicly documented.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: beta transitioning to production_ready. Achieved $100M ARR by December 2025 with widespread commercial use, but reviews note instability, bugs, and access limitations. Enterprise governance features are still developing. The Meta acquisition may accelerate enterprise hardening.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: Not applicable (Manus is closed-source). The community-built OpenManus recreation gained 16,000+ GitHub stars in 2 days, indicating massive interest. The open-source ai-manus project by Simpleyyt also exists on GitHub.
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: 2+ million users on waitlist within 7 days of March 2025 launch. Under 1% of waitlisted users received invite codes initially. 186,000+ Discord community members. $90M annualized revenue run rate reported August 2025. $100M ARR reported by December 2025, just 9 months after launch. Acquired by Meta for $2+ billion in December 2025.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: Freemium / subscription tiers. Plans include: Plus/Starter at $39/month, Pro at $199/month (some sources cite Base $99/month and Pro $499/month with unlimited usage), Enterprise with custom pricing. Free tier available during early testing phase. Estimated ~$2 per task cost.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: General-purpose autonomous task execution: (1) Software development — full-stack web apps, mobile apps, with one-click deployment; (2) Research and analysis — market research, competitive analysis, long-form reports; (3) Data analysis and visualization — charts, dashboards, statistical analysis; (4) Content creation — travel planning, bibliographic research, document generation; (5) Business operations — workflow automation via MCP integrations with enterprise tools (Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Stripe); (6) Academic and educational research.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Market leader in autonomous AI agents. Topped GAIA benchmark surpassing OpenAI Deep Research. Key differentiators vs competitors: (1) vs OpenAI Operator ($200/month) — more autonomous, better benchmark scores, one-click deployment; (2) vs Devin ($500/month) — broader use case coverage beyond coding, more affordable; (3) vs Claude Computer Use — fully autonomous vs interactive/guided; (4) vs ChatGPT — task execution vs conversational; (5) Unique one-click deployment capability. The $2B+ Meta acquisition validated its market position as a category-defining product. First mover in demonstrating that general-purpose AI agents can achieve commercial scale ($100M ARR in 9 months).

ecosystem_maturity.community_size: 186,000+ Discord members. 2+ million waitlisted users. Active reverse-engineering community (leaked system prompts, OpenManus project). The product generated significant developer and analyst attention globally upon launch.
ecosystem_maturity.documentation_quality: adequate. Official documentation at manus.im/docs covers basics, MCP connectors, and getting started. The influential 'Context Engineering for AI Agents' blog post by co-founder Peak Ji provides deep technical insights. However, documentation is still developing compared to mature developer platforms. Community resources supplement official docs.
ecosystem_maturity.third_party_integrations_count: 29+ built-in tools plus growing MCP connector ecosystem. Popular MCP connectors include Gmail, Notion, Stripe, HubSpot, Slack, Google Calendar, Hugging Face. Access to 1000+ community MCP servers. Community-built Manus MCP Server available for programmatic access.
ecosystem_maturity.tutorial_availability: Moderate. Official guides and templates available. Blog posts from Manus team (especially context engineering post). Numerous third-party tutorials, reviews, and analysis pieces from MIT Technology Review, VentureBeat, Medium, Dev.to, and various AI-focused publications. No formal course or certification program.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: autonomous (acts independently). Manus operates as a fully autonomous agent: users issue a goal, and the system independently plans, executes, verifies, and delivers results. Users can monitor via the 'Manus's Computer' interface but intervention is not required or expected.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Minimal explicit handoff. The system delivers completed results (reports, deployed applications, visualizations) to the user. The 'Manus's Computer' interface allows real-time observation, but there is no structured handoff protocol where the agent explicitly requests human input mid-task. Team collaboration (v1.5) allows multiple users to observe and interact with shared sessions.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Implicit through continued task refinement. Users can issue follow-up prompts to refine results. The event stream captures all interactions for potential learning. No publicly documented explicit feedback mechanism (e.g., thumbs up/down, RLHF from user interactions). The team rebuilt their framework four times based on learnings, suggesting strong internal iteration. [uncertain]

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Highly relevant for startup founders as both a tool and a case study. As a tool: Manus can replace junior analyst/developer capacity for research, prototyping, data analysis, and even full-stack app development at ~$39-199/month vs hiring. The one-click deployment feature is particularly valuable for MVPs. As a case study: Manus exemplifies the 'AI-native startup' playbook — from zero to $100M ARR in 9 months, $2B+ acquisition in under a year, with a team that prioritized product-market fit over building foundation models. Key lesson: wrapping existing LLMs (Claude, Qwen) with excellent agent orchestration and context engineering created more value than building new models. When to avoid: tasks requiring strict regulatory compliance (no SOC2/HIPAA), highly sensitive data processing (Chinese origin raises data sovereignty questions), or production-critical systems where bugs/instability cannot be tolerated.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: Strong buy signal for most startups. Cost-benefit: Manus at $39-199/month can replace significant human labor for research, prototyping, and development tasks. Building equivalent autonomous agent infrastructure would require 3-5 infra engineers and months of development (per E2B's estimate for sandbox infrastructure alone). However, consider building when: (1) you need full control over data and privacy (especially in regulated industries); (2) you need deep customization beyond what MCP connectors offer; (3) you need to integrate into existing agent frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI). Open-source alternatives like OpenManus exist for self-hosted needs but lack the polish and reliability of the commercial product. Post-Meta acquisition, vendor lock-in risk is a consideration.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — understanding Build vs Buy for AI agents, CRISP-DM applied to agent deployment) and Session 4 (AI business models & strategy — Manus as case study of $0-to-$100M-ARR AI-native business, unit economics of AI agents, Meta acquisition as exit strategy example).

confidence.data_quality: High. Information sourced from CNBC, Bloomberg, TechCrunch, MIT Technology Review, VentureBeat, official Manus blog, arxiv paper, and multiple credible tech publications. Acquisition details confirmed by WSJ, Reuters, Bloomberg, and official Manus blog post.
confidence.cross_reference: Meta acquisition price ($2B+) confirmed by CNBC, Bloomberg, CBC, Euronews, TechCrunch, and official Manus blog. GAIA benchmark scores confirmed across multiple sources (Helicone, Bind AI, BayTech Consulting). Revenue figures ($90M RRR Aug 2025, $100M ARR Dec 2025) reported by TechNode and multiple financial publications. Technical architecture details corroborated by arxiv paper (2505.02024v1), leaked system prompts, and official context engineering blog post. Chinese regulatory review confirmed by Bloomberg, SCMP, and multiple news outlets.
confidence.caveats: Rapidly evolving situation: (1) Meta acquisition under active Chinese regulatory review as of January 2026 — deal may face conditions or unwinding; (2) Post-acquisition integration with Meta's AI ecosystem will likely change product direction; (3) Pricing models have varied across sources and may have changed post-acquisition; (4) Some technical details come from leaked system prompts (March 2025) and may be outdated given subsequent versions; (5) The product's Chinese origin and Singapore relocation raise ongoing data sovereignty and geopolitical questions; (6) Enterprise readiness noted as a concern by some reviewers despite impressive revenue growth; (7) Valuation jumped from $500M (April 2025 Series B) to $2B+ acquisition (December 2025) in just 8 months, reflecting both genuine growth and AI market exuberance.
